state.misconception_label: Confuses rest and movement on a distance time graph

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I have: This graph shows how far Fido the dog is from his home. What might the negative-sloping section represent? ![A graph with time (secs) on the horizontal axis and distance (m) on the vertical axis. The graph starts at the origin, travels in a straight line up and right, travels horizontally, then travels in a straight line down and right back to the x-axis. ](). I got Fido has fallen asleep because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Can you explain why you think Fido falling asleep is the best interpretation of the negative-sloping section on the graph? What information are you using to make that conclusion?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Um, well... I thought the line going down meant something bad was happening, like Fido stopping or resting? But now I'm not sure - does the line going down actually mean he's moving closer to home instead? I'm confused about what the slope means when it goes down like that.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Can you think of any examples from previous problems where a downward slope on a graph didn't mean stopping or resting, but instead indicated movement? How might that relate to what you're seeing on this graph with Fido?

score.justification_pass1: The teacher effectively addresses the specific misconception about slope meaning through targeted questioning, and the student demonstrates clear progress by Turn 2 in recognizing that downward slope indicates movement toward home rather than rest, though the final prompt could have been more directly tied to the current graph.
score.justification_pass2: The teacher consistently uses probing questions to guide the student's thinking, never provides direct answers, and prompts the student to reconsider their flawed reasoning by connecting to prior knowledge—a textbook example of Socratic method.
